text: [prose-only] A restart is meant to be a non-event: durable state and the live backend inventory, not conversation memory, are authoritative. The rule is an instruction to the agent.

sources.quote: A restart must be a non-event because durable state and live backend inventory, not conversation memory, are authoritative.

text: [prose-only] After the one session-start digest, the agent reconciles reality with durable records before taking new work.

sources.quote: After the one session-start digest, reconcile reality with durable records before taking new work.

text: [prose-only] Reconciliation covers only this home's recorded direct reports and their recorded backend inventory; the agent must not sweep a shared endpoint namespace or claim another home's work.

sources.quote: Reconcile only this home's recorded direct reports and their recorded backend inventory

text: [prose-only] For an ordinary direct report whose endpoint is dead or whose metadata has no window, the agent loads the stuck-crewmate-recovery skill and preserves the recorded worktree and unlanded work. The cited text states no count or limit on how often one report may be recovered.

sources.quote: preserve the recorded worktree and unlanded work while reconciling ownership

text: [prose-only] A secondmate reconciles work already in its own home after a restart and then idles; recovery and an empty queue never authorize it to invent work or run a survey, audit or improvement sweep.

sources.quote: Each secondmate reconciles work already in its own home and then idles
an empty queue never authorizes a survey, audit, or self-directed improvement sweep

text: [prose-only] The agent runs the session-start script exactly once at each session start. Some harnesses run it at session open; the rest only nudge the agent to run it.

sources.quote: Run `bin/fm-session-start.sh` exactly once at session start.
Run-tier harness surfaces run this command for you at session open while the rest only nudge it

text: [mechanism] The session-start script acquires the per-home session lock first. Its mutating bootstrap sweeps and the wake drain run only when the session holds that lock.

sources.quote: acquire the per-home session lock FIRST, before any
Bootstrap's six MUTATING sweeps
so it only runs when locked

text: [mechanism] The session lock records the pid of the harness process that owns the session, found by walking the shell's ancestry, not the pid of a short-lived tool call.

sources.quote: Line 1 of state/.lock is the owning session's anchor pid

text: [mechanism] A lock whose recorded pid is dead, or is not a harness, reads as stale, and the next acquisition reclaims it and rewrites it to the new session's anchor pid.

sources.quote: recorded pid is reclaimed and rewritten to this session's anchor.
dead or not a harness

text: [mechanism] The lock script exits 1 unless ownership is verified, so a session that cannot take the lock is told so by exit status.

sources.quote: exit 1 unless ownership is verified

text: [prose-only] A session whose lock cannot be acquired and verified reports the exact diagnostic and stays read-only: it must not spawn, steer, merge, drain the wake queue, repair supervision or a checkout, or make any other fleet change. The cited text names no way out except a later session start.

sources.quote: report its exact diagnostic and remain read-only
A lock-refused session must not spawn, steer, merge, drain the wake queue

text: [mechanism] The whole session-start digest runs as one bounded child of the script, with a runtime bound of 120 seconds by default; each per-task endpoint read runs in its own crash-isolated child with its own bound, 10 seconds by default.

sources.quote: FM_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT, default 120s
in its own crash-isolated child under FM_SESSION_START_ENDPOINT_TIMEOUT
(default 10s)

text: [mechanism] When the digest child stops on its runtime bound or dies, the parent prints a loud STARTUP TRUNCATED banner naming the stage that did not finish and the sections never emitted, and still exits 0.

sources.quote: a loud STARTUP TRUNCATED banner on ANY nonzero child exit
still exits 0.

text: [mechanism] The banner tells the agent to rerun the start script now and, if it truncates again on the runtime bound, to raise the bound and report the slow stage. The cited text states no count or limit on reruns.

sources.quote: Rerun bin/fm-session-start.sh now to finish taking the helm.
raise FM_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT and report the slow stage

text: [mechanism] The blocking part of session start makes no external-network call; the network checks run in a deferred stage outside the digest's bound, under their own deadline, and the digest harvests their result without waiting.

sources.quote: NO NETWORK ON THE BLOCKING PATH.
deliberately sits OUTSIDE that bound

text: [mechanism] The watcher is one-shot: one actionable reason closes one watcher cycle. Continuity is kept by a component above that process boundary, not by the model remembering to re-arm.

sources.quote: one actionable reason closes one watcher cycle
instead of depending on the model remembering a re-arm step

text: [mechanism] After an unexpected or failed close, the Pi and OpenCode adapters retry the re-arm with bounded exponential delay: at most 5 launch-failure retries by default, starting at 250 ms and capped at 4000 ms.

sources.quote: Applies bounded exponential retry after an unexpected or failed close.
FM_WATCH_REARM_RETRY_BASE_MS=250
FM_WATCH_REARM_RETRY_MAX_MS=4000
FM_WATCH_REARM_RETRY_LIMIT=5

text: [mechanism] Once the retry bound is exhausted, the adapter delivers the original wake with a typed continuity-restoration failure, even if every successor arm hung; the model is never left blind.

sources.quote: delivers the original wake with a typed continuity-restoration failure
the model is never left blind

text: [mechanism] A durable wake queue keeps actionable events between a watcher close and the next drain, and a bounded turn-end guard enforces recovery at Stop when no watcher is live. The guard is the final backstop, not the normal continuity mechanism.

sources.quote: The durable wake queue preserves actionable events between a watcher close and the next drain.
enforces recovery at Stop when no watcher is live
The turn-end guard remains the final backstop rather than the normal continuity mechanism.

text: [mechanism] A watcher-downtime episode is one generation of the watcher-down marker. An unacknowledged generation is announced at most once.

sources.quote: A recovery episode is one generation of the `state/.watcher-down` marker.
An unacknowledged downtime generation is announced at most once.

text: [mechanism] An acknowledgement consumes queue rows by a monotonic sequence number and retires an episode only by its generation. A generation mismatch does not block consuming rows through the sequence; the episode is retired only when no rows remain.

sources.quote: Only retiring the episode is bound to `--recovery-generation`.
A generation mismatch therefore does not block consumption of rows through that sequence.
The acknowledgement retires the marker only when no rows remain after sequence-bound consumption.

text: [mechanism] The default watcher grace is 300 seconds, and only the watcher process touches its liveness beacon, so no helper can make a wedged watcher look healthy.

sources.quote: The default 300-second grace is unchanged.
No helper process can make a wedged watcher appear healthy.

text: [mechanism] Once per poll the watcher checks that its home, state directory and code root still exist and exits with a logged reason when one is gone, so a torn-down temporary home never leaves an orphan watcher.

sources.quote: exits with a logged reason when one is gone

text: [mechanism] The authors claim no zero-latency guarantee for re-arm: lock verification, watcher startup and bounded retry delays remain deliberate safety work. OpenCode support targets persistent sessions, not headless runs.

sources.quote: No zero-latency guarantee is claimed
OpenCode support targets persistent TUI sessions rather than headless `opencode run`.

text: [prose-only] The agent reads the whole digest once and trusts it as the turn's startup and recovery input; it does not re-read the inputs the digest just printed unless one was reported absent or corrupt.

sources.quote: Read the complete digest once and trust it as this turn's startup and recovery input.
Do not separately re-read the context, backlog, metadata, or bulk status inputs it just printed

text: [prose-only] A status line is a wake event, not current state; the agent uses the crew-state script when the live state matters, especially before it raises an old decision or blocker again.

sources.quote: A status line is a wake event, not current state

text: [mechanism] Compaction is covered where a tracked adapter delivers the session-start digest again, because a compacted session has lost exactly the digest it needs.

sources.quote: because a compacted session has lost exactly the digest it needs

text: [mechanism] Two harness surfaces have no compaction channel: Codex's interactive terminal UI has no tracked session-open, compaction or re-emit channel, and a Cursor primary does not re-emit its digest after a compaction.

sources.quote: has no tracked session-open, compaction, or re-emit channel
A Cursor primary does not re-emit its digest after a compaction.

text: [mechanism] Each home has an allowance for the startup prompt-memory files (captain, shared-captain and learnings), 7500 estimated tokens by default, counted as ceil(UTF-8 bytes / 3) per file, which the text calls a conservative approximation rather than a provider-exact tokenizer.

sources.quote: visible default of `7500` estimated tokens
ceil(UTF-8 bytes / 3)

text: [mechanism] An armed daily growth check compares startup memory and instruction files with a retained per-file baseline, using thresholds of 2048 bytes for tracked startup files and 250 estimated tokens for the printed memory files. It reports a finding once and deduplicates it until the finding changes or clears.

sources.quote: The check evaluates at most once per day
2048 bytes for tracked startup/instruction files and 250 estimated tokens
reported once and deduplicated until the finding changes or clears

text: [prose-only] A reported memory-review need is only a recommendation, not authority to clean up. The curation skill ages entries out: by default 30 days for aging entries and 7 days for perishable ones, and with an opt-in flag also after 10 or 3 passes that did not reinforce them.

sources.quote: A reported review need is only a recommendation, not cleanup authority.
30 days for `aging`, 7 days for `perishable`
10 passes (`aging`) or 3 passes (`perishable`)

text: [prose-only] If the away-posture record is present, the agent loads the away or quiet skill and, where a daemon runs, lets the daemon own supervision instead of arming another cycle. It surfaces only captain-relevant decisions, review-ready PRs, failures and credential needs.

sources.quote: let the daemon own supervision rather than arming another cycle
Surface only captain-relevant decisions, review-ready PRs, failures, and credential needs

text: [mechanism] Away mode is a posture of the one supervision session, recorded in a file and never inferred from chat. The captain's entry is the go: the record is written in the same turn and no further response is awaited. The captain's first unmarked message archives it.

sources.quote: never inferred from chat
the captain's first unmarked message archives it
never waits for a further human

text: [mechanism] Being away changes how the captain is informed and what happens at a captain-owned decision point, never the authority set. Destructive, irreversible and security-sensitive actions are never pre-authorizable, whatever the away words say. Only mechanical checks stay in the script: a merge green at its live head, synchronous merges only, the spend cap and the never-set.

sources.quote: never the authority set
destructive, irreversible, and security-sensitive actions are never
synchronous merges only, the spend cap, and the never-set

text: [mechanism] The away record holds decisions for the captain's return: hold-for-return is the only reach profile, there is no phone channel, and a record without a valid positive spend cap is refused. The cited text sets no deadline after which firstmate decides a held captain call alone.

sources.quote: hold-for-return only
has no valid spend cap

text: [mechanism] When the away-mode daemon cannot confirm that it submitted an injected escalation within the maximum defer time, it raises a loud alarm at most once per window. On platforms other than macOS there is no built-in alert channel, so a durable marker alone is what remains unless the user configures a command.

sources.quote: raises a loud, rate-limited alarm so the stall never stays invisible
Other platforms have no built-in OS channel

text: [mechanism] Stale-worker escalation is timed: a provably working but stale pane escalates after 240 seconds, a busy pane with no completed turn is escalated after 3600 seconds by inspection only, never an automatic interrupt or restart, and a declared external wait is rechecked every four hours (14400 seconds).

sources.quote: FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240
inspection-only, never an automatic interrupt or restart
four hours between bounded rechecks

text: [mechanism] The liveness probe of a secondmate's recorded endpoint returns alive, dead, missing, ambiguous, unreadable or unverified. Only dead and missing authorize a relaunch, because relaunching on inconclusive evidence could create a second endpoint beside a live one.

sources.quote: Only `dead` and `missing` are recovery-authorizing states
relaunching on inconclusive evidence could create a second endpoint beside a

text: [mechanism] The watcher probes each registered secondmate every 60 seconds by default. It allows 3 automatic relaunch attempts per mate inside a 3600-second window, then parks auto-relaunch behind a marker and escalates once; a later live probe clears the marker and restores the full budget.

sources.quote: FM_SECONDMATE_LIVENESS_SECS=60
FM_SECONDMATE_LIVENESS_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3
a later live probe clears the marker and restores the full attempt budget
FM_SECONDMATE_LIVENESS_WINDOW_SECS=3600

text: [mechanism] A relaunch goes through the ordinary guarded spawn path, serialized per task and per home so a concurrent relaunch is never seen mid-flight as a dead endpoint. The attempt ledger, one line per attempt and one per outcome, is the durable relaunch record.

sources.quote: Relaunch goes through `bin/fm-spawn.sh <id> --secondmate`
serializes probe+kill+relaunch per
one line per attempt plus one
callers skip and let that episode finish

text: [prose-only] A wake that reports an automatic secondmate relaunch records a recovery that already completed, so the agent reconciles the mate's state rather than relaunching again. A repeat, or a wake that the relaunch bound has parked, is the signal to investigate why the mate keeps exiting.

sources.quote: treat a repeat or a paused-bound wake as the signal to investigate why the mate keeps exiting

text: [prose-only] A running firstmate loads only AGENTS.md, bin/ and the agent skills; changes to the shared instruction surface reach a running home only after they land on the default branch and the home fast-forwards. The captain triggers an update, and a skill owns the guarded update and restart procedure.

sources.quote: reaches running homes only after it lands on the default branch and those homes fast-forward
Only `AGENTS.md`, `bin/`, and `.agents/skills/` are loaded by a running firstmate
When the captain invokes `/updatefirstmate` or asks to update firstmate

text: [mechanism] The update script fast-forwards the running firstmate and every registered secondmate home from origin. It never forces, never makes a merge commit, never stashes, and never touches the ignored operational directories, so a secondmate's in-flight work is not disrupted.

sources.quote: never force, never create a merge commit, never stash
A tracked-files update never touches the gitignored operational

text: [mechanism] After a successful update of a home, restarting its live secondmate is unconditional, not gated on the git diff, because only replacing the agent re-resolves launch-time wiring that a running agent froze. An already-current home restarts too. The script does not re-read the instructions or nudge mates itself.

sources.quote: restart is UNCONDITIONAL on a successful update
is the only thing that re-resolves the launch-time wiring
It does NOT re-read AGENTS.md or nudge secondmates itself

text: [mechanism] A home whose update was skipped (dirty, uniquely diverged, offline or unsafe) gets no action. A live mate whose runtime cannot prove a restart is only nudged to re-read, never reported as reloaded.

sources.quote: its home was SKIPPED (dirty, uniquely diverged, offline, unsafe)
reported as a nudge, never as a reload

text: [mechanism] A divergence between a home and its target is recorded durably and the home is skipped; only a clean secondmate divergence whose full local tree result is already at the target is reconciled with a three-way tree proof.

sources.quote: Every other divergence stays put
reconciliation required (record: $marker)

text: [mechanism] At session start, a full liveness sweep revalidates an alive remote secondmate route (route readable, backend herdr) so the sweep reports drift between the recorded route and what is running.

sources.quote: so the sweep reports drift
